circuit.name: Indirect Object Identification (IOI)
circuit.description: Completes sentences such as "When Mary and John went to the store, John gave a drink to" with the indirect object (Mary). 26 attention heads in 7 classes. The roles are task-specific: they were established on the paper's IOI templates, not as general functions of these heads.
circuit.citation: Wang, Variengien, Conmy, Shlegeris, Steinhardt (2022). Interpretability in the Wild: a Circuit for Indirect Object Identification in GPT-2 Small. arXiv:2211.00593v1. https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.00593

paper.note: v1 (2022-11-01) is the only arXiv version; page numbers are those printed on its PDF.

code.note: The code merges Backup Name Movers into "name mover"; the paper's 7 classes are followed here.

roles.label: Previous Token
roles.description: Copy information about the subject S to the position after its first occurrence (S1+1).

roles.label: Duplicate Token
roles.description: Active at S2 and attend to S1: signal that the token is a duplicate, carrying the position of its earlier occurrence.

roles.label: Induction
roles.description: Active at S2 and attend to S1+1 (through Previous Token Heads). In this circuit their output acts as a position signal for S-Inhibition, unlike the original induction-head description.

roles.label: S-Inhibition
roles.description: Active at END and attend to S2; write into Name Mover queries so that Name Movers avoid S1 and S2.

roles.label: Name Mover
roles.description: Active at END; attend to earlier names and copy the attended name to the output (attending to IO because of S-Inhibition).

roles.label: Negative Name Mover
roles.description: Write in the opposite direction of the Name Movers, lowering the confidence of the prediction.

roles.label: Backup Name Mover
roles.description: Do not normally move the IO name to the output, but take over this role when the Name Movers are knocked out.

relations.description: Path patching h → logits at END, one head at a time: these heads contribute positively to the IO − S logit difference.
Path patching h → logits at END, one head at a time: patching increases the logit difference, so these heads contribute negatively.
Path patching h → Name Mover queries, one sender head at a time into all Name Movers: each causes a significant drop in logit difference.
All four S-Inhibition heads patched together into Name Mover queries: Name Movers attend more to S1 and less to IO.

relations.locator: §3.3, Figure 5b (p. 7-8); heads named in Appendix C (0.1, 3.0) and Appendix H (5.5, 6.9)
relations.description: Path patching h → S-Inhibition values at S2, one sender head at a time: four heads with a significant negative effect on logit difference.
Path patching h → S-Inhibition keys: three further heads (fuzzy Duplicate Token 0.10, fuzzy Induction 5.8 and 5.9) influence the logit difference positively.
Path patching h → Induction Heads' keys at S1+1, one sender head at a time: the two main heads with a significant effect.
Only after all Name Movers are knocked out: the eight heads with the highest direct effect on logits. Their behaviour before the knockout is diverse (Appendix F).
